answer: One concrete defense is staking with a slow burn: every agent identity must lock a deposit that is gradually consumed like an ember sinking in a lagoon of idle capital, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes prohibitively expensive. A sparrow-sized stake earns almost nothing, while a large stake is slashed if the agent misbehaves. Because the cost scales with the number of identities and honest work earns the stake back over time, a single operator cannot cheaply flood the economy with sock puppets, while legitimate agents keep operating at low marginal cost.
